# Pinned petite-vue source

`petite-vue-svg.html` is the complete unmodified `examples/svg.html` from the
existing petite-vue gitlink at `9ff3b98b844033b935143c221176c81244aae32e`.

- [Original source](https://github.com/vuejs/petite-vue/blob/9ff3b98b844033b935143c221176c81244aae32e/examples/svg.html)
- Git blob: `2d403f834520e4cf8565691d1b68fd1968c1295a`
- Bytes: `2495`
- SHA-256: `e89e754aba3960ad9891859de667cbe8485955c8b27e72dc0a48614d16288f4a`
- License: the adjacent unmodified `petite-vue-LICENSE` from the same commit.

The native law observes the complete original Document lexer run, authored
tag/interpolation spans and unchanged raw script/style bytes. It proves no
petite-vue runtime, `v-scope` meaning, DOM tree policy or L2/product completion.

`html-structure.tsv` contains twelve original explicit-envelope HTML law sources.
Each row records actual HTML local names and parent start-tag order. Native Rust
structure laws and the existing Chromium browser suite consume the same bytes
and census. The admitted provider proves only element ancestry, case folding,
true void insertion and ignored nonvoid slashes for its documented subset.
Text DOM values, general tree policies and petite-vue stay unfinished;
the complete pinned SVG document deliberately refuses structural admission.

Four additional sources retain actual once-decoded character-reference payloads,
including numeric/named HTML whitespace before and between envelope members.
Their element ancestry and no-quirks mode are checked by the same browser suite.

`html-attributes.json` keeps ten complete original sources and effective static
attribute name/value arrays in start-tag order. Native owner-bound receipts and
actual Chromium DOMParser consume the same bytes, including escaped authored
CRLF/CR/NUL and reference boundaries. ASCII folding, normalized-name first
duplicates, empty/Boolean/unquoted values and complete once-decoded references
are covered. This gives no URL/property, Vue directive or petite-vue meaning.

`html-body-nodes.json` retains fifteen complete original sources and whole
direct body-subtree child-node arrays. Twelve sources admit original text,
ordinary comments and elements; three characterize actual browser text
reinsertion after body/html and require explicit native body-node refusal.
The same bytes execute in native Rust and actual Chromium. Literal/reference
line boundaries, ignored text NULL versus comment replacement, literal comment
reference spellings, empty/long-hyphen comments, Unicode, once-only payloads,
void/nonvoid insertion and nested original parents are covered. General HTML
tree policies, outer node modes and petite-vue semantics remain unfinished.

`html-body-void-elements.json` contains ten complete original sources and
independently authored whole ancestry, effective attribute and direct-node
packets. Native Rust and actual Chromium compare the same packets for
`area`, `embed`, `source`, `track` and `wbr`, including empty child views,
nested original parents, slash/case forms and following text/comment/sibling
boundaries. The existing body void family is an unchanged-semantics control.
This is bounded Document structure, without petite-vue meaning or a product
route switch; general insertion policies and obsolete void tags remain open.

`html-semantic-body-containers.json` and `html-semantic-body-nesting.json` keep
ten complete original sources and whole ancestry, effective attributes and
direct child-node packets for `article`, `aside`, `footer`, `header`, `main`,
`nav` and `section`. The independently authored packets execute in native Rust
and actual Chromium, including seven mixed-case/slash names, normalized
attribute duplicates, harmless `xmlns` attributes, literal/reference CRLF/NUL,
complete sibling and nested parent boundaries, and an existing-tag control.
All containers require explicit matching ends; implied-end/table transitions,
foreign breakouts, formatting elements and Vue syntax remain refused.

`html-semantic-body-frames.json` independently records every admitted semantic
container's exact authored opening/closing bytes and ignored-slash flag. Native
Rust compares the whole frame packet, including case, CRLF/NUL and attribute
spelling; it does not infer an expected slash from a suffix of actual output.

`html-grouping-body-containers.json` keeps eight complete original sources and
whole ancestry, effective attributes, direct child nodes and authored frames
for `address`, `blockquote`, `figure`, `figcaption`, `hgroup` and `search`.
Native Rust and actual Chromium consume the same packets. Every admitted case
uses explicit matching ends; the existing implied-end, table, foreign-breakout,
formatting and Vue-syntax refusals remain authoritative.

`html-special-text.json` retains eight complete explicit-envelope sources and
whole ancestry, effective attributes and direct child nodes for head `script`
and body `title`/`style`/`script`/`textarea`. The same packet executes against
actual Chromium, the shipped document parser and native L1. RAWTEXT versus
RCDATA entity handling, ASCII-folded ends, pseudo script closes and the HTML
textarea first-newline rule (literal LF, CRLF and a decoded reference) are
covered. Slashed special-text starts, Vue interpolation and literal NULL stay
typed refusals where the retained lexer or the two oracles do not agree.

`html-implied-ends-and-tables.json` keeps twelve complete original sources and
whole ancestry, effective attributes and direct child nodes for implied end
tags (`p`, list items, `dt`/`dd`, ruby text, `option`/`optgroup`) and the
table insertion modes. Native Rust and actual Chromium consume the same
packets; native Rust also pins each element closed without an authored end
tag. Implied starts, fostered content, table text, ignored tags and
parse-error ends keep typed refusals.

`html-select.json` retains sixteen complete sources: fourteen bounded native
select packets and two actual browser trees whose parse-error recovery native
construction explicitly refuses. Whole ancestry, effective attributes and
direct child nodes execute in Rust and Chromium; native laws also pin every
original tag callback and exact UTF-8 opening/closing span. Four customizable
select packets additionally match the shipped parser for nested phrasing,
options, semantic lists, tables and special text. Omitted option/group ends, hr
separation, table-cell context, case/slashes, static duplicates, decoded values
and outside-select nesting are explicit. Nested select/input recovery remains a
typed refusal; the prior thirteen source packets keep their authored bytes.

`html-foreign-content.json` retains fourteen complete browser packets. Ten
bounded packets admit explicit SVG/MathML subtrees, canonical SVG element and
attribute adjustments, foreign self-closing elements, SVG and MathML HTML
integration points, nested foreign roots, table-cell context and original
text/comment/reference values. Nine of those packets also match the shipped
document parser's complete namespace/parent/direct-node tree. Four browser
packets retain typed native refusals where that parser and Chromium disagree
about integration-point spelling or nonvoid slashes, where HTML breakout
recovery would move nodes, or where the retained lexer hides SVG-title markup.
Native Rust and actual Chromium consume every complete packet; no DOM result is
derived from native output. CDATA, annotation-xml HTML integration, arbitrary
foreign names and complete adoption/raw-text/template policies remain open.
